experiment: E3 — multi-GPU: pipeline parallel (layer split) vs tensor split (-ts 50/50), prefill + decode at S=65k/131k/262k, both RTX 5060 Ti (ROADMAP block 6)
status: prepared: code and grid ready; run not executed — waiting for user launch (both cards must be FREE, the chat backend will disconnect during the run)

runner.build: llama.cpp b11819 (v0.7.0-dev), win-x64, CUDA 13.4 prebuilt; -ts and comma-separated multi-device confirmed by --help probes on 23.10.2026

model.arch: L=48; 40 local SWA (window=1024) + 8 global full-attn; vocab=262144, lm_head tied

gpu.devices: both RTX 5060 Ti 16 GiB: CUDA0 (display) + CUDA1 (non-display), VMM: yes on both
gpu.requirement: close BOTH LM Studio instances before the run (the chat backend lives on GPU0 — the session will disconnect during the run, bat works unattended; restart LM Studio afterwards)

modes.PP: -dev CUDA0,CUDA1 -sm layer (pipeline parallel: layers distributed across the cards sequentially). Physics expectation: decode batch=1 is NOT accelerated (same total volume read, just from two buses in sequence); prefill ~2x minus overhead
modes.TS: -dev CUDA0,CUDA1 -ts 50/50 (tensor split: each GEMM matrix cut across the cards). Physics expectation: per-token weight reads halved from each card -> decode ~2x minus allreduce-overhead; prefill ~2x. This is the ROADMAP block 6 measurement

grid.repetitions: prefill: r=2 for S<=131072, r=1 at 262144; decode: r=2 everywhere

metrics.primary_prefill: `pp{S}` line (t/s ± std) — prefill TPS in each mode
metrics.primary_decode: `tg64 @ d{S}` line (TPS ± std) — decode TPS after an S prefix; comparison with E2 numbers on a single card = win/loss from parallelism
metrics.comparison_baseline: E2-long-context-prefill (single CUDA1 card, same S and f16 KV)

time_estimate: ~2-4 hours (overnight): prefill_flops at tflops_eff≈30 TFLOPS on ONE card ~68/173/497 s; PP/TS roughly twice as fast, but decode cells do their own prefill outside the timing window

preflights_in_bat: B: -m fake model -dev CUDA0,CUDA1 → 'invalid device' = fail; checks multi-device syntax (~2 s, no VRAM)
C: real PP cell f16 S=512 r=1 — findstr 'Device 1' (both cards initialized) + exit 0 (short VRAM on both)
D: real TS cell f16 S=512 r=1 -ts 50/50 — exit 0; checks that tensor split is accepted by the runner
launch_protocol.logging: raw/run_log.txt: timestamp + exact command line + exit code of each cell; raw/pp_{mode}_f16_S{S}.txt and tg_d{S}_{mode}_f16.txt — full cell output
user_steps: 1. Close BOTH LM Studio instances (the Qwen Code session will disconnect during the run)
2. Double-click experiments/E3-multi-gpu-tp-ts/run_e3.bat (the console must stay open)
3. Wait for 'E3 done' (estimate 2-4 h); then restart LM Studio
launch_protocol.note: QWEN_NO_PAUSE=1 disables pause; OOM/cell failure does not drop the grid — bat continues, exit code in run_log/raw

deliverables_5_files_protocol: table.md (table: S × mode {PP,TS} -> pp t/s and tg64 TPS; comparison columns with single-card E2)
plot.png (pp/tg TPS(S) for PP vs TS vs single-GPU E2)
conclusion.md (findings: where tensor split wins over PP and a single card, communication overhead; C-xx in CONCLUSIONS.md after the measurement)
